Attempted verbatim-quote audit: every quote in this file was checked as an exact substring against its own re-fetched raw source text; WebFetch-derived paraphrases that failed this check were re-sourced from raw HTML or dropped
absences: Zeno Power CTO/co-founder Jake Matthews (named in the task brief) does not appear anywhere on zenopower.com/our-team as of this pass -- searched twice, confirmed absent from both leadership and advisory-board sections. Not included as a current leader; his prior CTO status could not be confirmed as still current, and no departure announcement was found either. Flagged rather than guessed.

No verbatim, attributed TRISO price ($/kg or $/MTU) or capacity fee could be found from any Standard Nuclear executive -- the S-1/424B4 gives aggregate dollar figures (backlog, pipeline, SAM/TAM) and per-facility MTU/year throughput, but never a specific per-unit or per-kg fuel price in an executive's own words.

Standard Nuclear's own HALEU sourcing is structurally ambiguous across sources: the 424B4 describes 'customer-provided feedstock' as the default model, while ANS Nuclear Newswire and World Nuclear News both state Standard Nuclear is 'among the companies receiving HALEU from the DOE' directly (the Jan 2026 shipment was DOE-allotted to customer Radiant, then physically delivered to Standard Nuclear for processing). Both facts are reported as true in this file; no single source reconciles them into one clean sentence.

GeekWire, Forbes (initial attempt), and Axios blocked automated fetches (HTTP 403) on first try for several Zeno Power and TerraPower articles; GeekWire's 'Inside the kitchen where Zeno Power tests radioisotope recipes' and the Axios hyperscaler-nuclear piece on Chris Levesque were never successfully read and contain no quotes here as a result (Forbes was eventually reached on a retry with --compressed and is used).

Nuclear Barbarians' 'TRISO Serious ft. Kurt Terrani' (Aug 2025) and Atomic Insights' 'Atomic Show #333' (June 2025) are the two known long-form audio interviews with Kurt Terrani in this window; neither publishes a fetchable transcript (Substack serves a JS shell to non-browser clients; Atomic Insights' page is show notes only, no transcript).

A Chris Levesque quote on Natrium's HALEU dependency ('Natrium will run on HALEU for the life of the plant,' POWER Magazine) was found and verified verbatim but dated November 2021 -- before the 2024-08 window start -- and was dropped rather than misdated.

A verbatim, timestamped SVI Radio interview with Chris Levesque (March 30, 2026) contains genuine in-window schedule commentary, but the page's transcript UI embeds a '(m:ss)' timestamp marker roughly every 10-15 words, so no clean multi-clause quote could be extracted without stripping non-verbal markup; dropped rather than published a quote requiring that transformation.

No quote from Zeno Power co-founder/COO Jonathan Segal was found anywhere in the window; he appears only in leadership listings and a 2025 alumni-newsletter coffee-chat recap with no direct quotations.

quotes.quote: China is currently operating on the moon with a radioisotope power system, whereas the U.S. lander is using solar-powered batteries,
quotes.what_it_means: Bernstein frames Zeno's NASA/Intuitive Machines/Blue Origin lunar work explicitly as catching up to a Chinese capability gap, not just a technology demonstration -- said around the company's $50 million Series B (bringing total funding to $70 million), with a stated goal of full-scale system demonstrations in 2026 and first commercial deliveries in 2027.

quotes.speaker: Tyler Bernstein
quotes.quote: As demand for long-duration lunar infrastructure grows, we are building the production capacity to support future commercial and government missions.
quotes.what_it_means: Announced alongside a commercial payload agreement with Firefly Aerospace to fly a Zeno radioisotope heater unit on a Blue Ghost lunar mission (no earlier than 2028) -- Zeno explicitly ties a single space demonstration to a broader production-capacity buildout claim, its version of the same demonstration-to-commercial-scale narrative Standard Nuclear and Antares use for terrestrial TRISO fuel.

quotes.speaker: Chris Levesque
quotes.quote: To successfully address growing energy demand, we must deploy gigawatts of advanced nuclear energy in the 2030s. This agreement with Meta is designed to support the rapid deployment of our Natrium technology that provides the reliable, flexible, and carbon-free power our country needs,
quotes.what_it_means: The Meta agreement covers up to eight Natrium plants (up to 2.8 GW baseload, boostable to 4 GW using Natrium's molten-salt storage) -- the largest single commercial commitment in the Natrium program's history, and the clearest sign yet that hyperscaler data-center demand, not the original ARDP demonstration mandate, is now driving TerraPower's order book.
